extracted.intended_audience: general readers and journalists interested in investigative and collaborative data journalism
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ), describing its history, major investigations, collaborative model, data/technology practices, governance, funding, and impact. Useful for readers seeking how ICIJ conducts large-scale cross-border investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative journalism model
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ's collaborative journalism model has been described as a new departure for global journalism that embraces collaboration. ICIJ's cross-border collaboration involves more than 140 newspapers, television and radio stations, and online media organizations, and is marked by transparency and peer scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes transparency and peer scrutiny; projects are produced by large international partnerships; stories resulting from collaboration are published simultaneously around the world and made available to readers free. The model values broad partner participation and synchronized global release to maximise impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and duration of investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Major ICIJ investigations often span years and involve processing millions of documents and records (e.g., the Panama Papers: journalists spent a year sifting through 11.5 million leaked files; Pandora Papers: 11.9 million documents / 2.9 TB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations require long planning and execution timelines, extensive cross-organizational coordination, and resources to process terabytes of structured and unstructured data (emails, PDFs, images, spreadsheets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specialist personnel (data journalists & programmers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The data-intensive projects involved not just veteran investigative journalists, but also demanded data journalists and programmers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful projects integrate multidisciplinary teams — investigative reporters plus data analysts, programmers and technologists — to manage, analyze and interpret large datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management and analysis technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ adopted technologies to manage international collaboration on terabytes of data and to extract meaningful information; among the technologies used were the Neo4j graph database management system and Linkurious to search and visualize the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice includes use of graph databases and visualization tools for relationship-mapping; tooling choices should support searching, visualizing and linking entities across massive datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-source research platforms (Datashare)
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ's research platform is called Datashare. It is free and open source. Datashare was developed by ICIJ together with EPFL; in 2021 Datashare was improved to make 11.9 million records (2.9 terabytes) available to more than 600 journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing tools and data-sharing platforms should be open, scalable, and enable broad access for vetted journalists; maintaining repositories and releases (with versioning) is part of the infrastructure for collaborative investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking and verification tooling (Prophecies)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2021, the ICIJ's technology team built a new open-source platform, Prophecies, to make data fact-checking more efficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in tooling that streamlines verification workflows for large datasets; dedicated fact-checking platforms can improve efficiency and reliability of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public databases and machine-learning analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ's public Offshore Leaks Database is a repository of information on companies registered in tax havens. It uses machine-learning techniques to analyze data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making derived datasets publicly searchable and applying ML techniques for entity resolution/analysis are part of ICIJ's approach; also provide guidance and research assistance to partners on use of public databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships with major media organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ partnered with major outlets (e.g., The Guardian, BBC, Le Monde, The Washington Post, Süddeutsche Zeitung, NDR) and hundreds of journalists across many media organisations to produce investigations like the Panama Papers and Pandora Papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-scale impact relies on coordinated partnerships across high-profile media organisations to share workload, expertise, and distribution; selection and coordination of partners is a practical criterion for project reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication practice: simultaneous worldwide release and free access
rubrics_metrics.description: The stories that result from the collaboration are published simultaneously around the world and made available to readers free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synchronized global publication maximizes impact and reduces the chance of selective reporting; making outputs freely accessible supports transparency and public accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance, independence and nonprofit status
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ was spun off into a fully independent organisation governed by a board of directors, an Advisory Committee, and the ICIJ Network Committee, and was granted 501(c)(3) nonprofit status in 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational independence, transparent governance structures and nonprofit status are presented as foundations for impartial investigative work and for attracting funding/support while maintaining editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding transparency and donors
rubrics_metrics.description: The ICIJ is funded by donations. Financial supporters include the Adessium Foundation, the Bertha Foundation, the National Endowment for Democracy and the Open Society Foundations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosing funding sources and maintaining donation-supported models is part of organizational transparency; awareness of funders is relevant to assessments of potential influences and sustainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact metrics: legal/policy outcomes and recovered revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ investigations have helped bring about legislation (e.g., the Corporate Transparency Act; Enablers Act proposals), and governments have recovered more than US$1.36 billion in taxes as a result of the Panama Papers project alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact can be measured by concrete policy changes, legal actions, recovered public funds, and other systemic outcomes resulting from investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and awards as credibility indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: ICIJ's collaborations have received several awards, including the 2017 Pulitzer Prize for Explanatory Reporting, News Emmys, nominations for the Nobel Peace Prize, and other journalism prizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major industry awards and recognitions are used as signals of investigative quality and impact; award history provides an external validation metric.
